text:
linh: Brain dump: prototype for a console 'quick contingency' action — single-row control to apply common fallback modes during noisy rollouts. Aim: <30s operator flow, minimal knobs, full audit trail. Thoughts? :sparkles:
devon: Love the single-row UX. Key constraint: it must tie to the active rollout (which model/route) so operators don't accidentally affect unrelated traffic. Show the route/model name in the row.
sara: Agree. Also show live signal matches (eg: 5xx rate, median latency, quota breaches). Operators want the reason visible at glance.
kat: UX golden rule: show 'what will change' and 'how long' upfront. I suggest Mode (soft-throttle | quarantine | fallback-model) + Duration presets + Severity slider (low/medium/high).
mike: Add an immediate 'estimated impact' badge: cost delta and expected p99 latency change. We have enough telemetry to estimate that.
linh: Good. MVP controls: Mode dropdown, Duration (30s/2m/10m/custom), Severity (brief tooltip: affects how strict matching is), Silent checkbox (no notif to downstream teams).
james: Auditability note: each apply must record actor, reason, matched-signal snapshot id, deterministic event id. Backend should emit deterministic breadcrumb ids like: contingency:2026-03-22T15:00:00Z:route-123. Avoid ephemeral uuids so decision-simulator can replay exactly.
kat: Also require a short freeform 'reason' when severity increases or mode escalates. Put a 140-char limit. Save that verbatim in the audit row.
linh: Example audit payload I'll propose in the RFC (plain-text JSON block for engineers):
```
{"event":"contingency_apply","actor":"linh","route":"/v1/generate","mode":"fallback-model","severity":"high","duration":"2m","reason":"prod us-east 5xx spike","breadcrumb":"contingency:2026-03-22T15:00:00Z:route-123"}
```
kat: UI should also show a human-friendly line: "Applied fallback-model for /v1/generate (2m) — reason: 5xx spike in us-east — see traces" with a link to sample traces.
sara: Ops process question: do we allow undo from the quick row? I vote yes: an immediate 'revert' button that sends a short audit note. Reverts should be rate-limited (no more than 3 in 10m) to avoid oscillation.
mike: Backend needs to compute estimated query delta for each mode (eg quarantine -> +40% invocations, fallback-model -> -10% cost but +5ms latency). Expose these as small inline numbers so operator can choose.
james: For the decision-simulator replay we need two things in the event: the deterministic breadcrumb id and a snapshot pointer to the sampled telemetry object (not full payload inline). That pointer can be a short token like tb-20260322-0007.
ops-bot: Preview build deployed: https://console-preview.internal/quick-contingency?pr=1317 (contains simulated traffic and a "view matched signals" flyout).
linh: Nice. One more idea: when matched signals include specific error classes (eg prompt-safety / hallucination classifier), show an inline "attach repro set" checkbox so we capture the failing prompts to help model team debug.
kat: Final UI nit: sort matched signals by estimated severity impact, and show a tiny chevron to expand raw counts.
sara: Sounds actionable. Linh, can you draft a 1-pager RFC with: mockups, telemetry contract (breadcrumb + snapshot token), backend id format, required audit fields, and revert/rate-limit policy? I'll slot it for the ops sync.
linh: On it. I'll include the mock, the example audit payload above, the breadcrumb/id format, and the list of required inline estimates (cost delta, latency delta, invocation delta). Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
